q: An antique mourning brooch in the Natural History Museum collection contains five real examples of which animals?
d: The specimens were blackened to give the jewelry a suitably somber appearance. The museum identifies them as Polychalca punctatissima.
evidence: Museum curator describes antique mourning brooch with five Polychalca punctatissima specimens deliberately blackened for funereal appearance.

q: A sixteenth-century football recovered at Stirling Castle held its air inside which animal organ?
d: Stitched leather panels enclosed the inflatable bladder. The ball was found behind roof paneling; any personal connection to Mary, Queen of Scots remains uncertain.

q: The violin beetle’s dramatically flattened body helps it hunt in which tight space?
d: Its thin shape lets it enter cracks and crevices where it finds prey. The broad, unusual outline also gives the beetle its musical-instrument nickname.
